name: Alabama

sales.rateNote: General state sales and use tax rate. Reduced state rates apply to food/groceries (2%), automotive sales (2%), manufacturing and farm machinery (1.5%). Cities and counties add their own sales taxes.

local.levies: city and county sales, use, rental and lodgings taxes; ALDOR administers over 200 local sales taxes, others are self-administered by the locality; cities may also levy a police-jurisdiction (PJ) rate, typically half the corporate-limits rate

groceries.note: State rate on food/groceries is 2% since September 1, 2025 (3% from Sept. 1, 2023 to Aug. 31, 2025). City and county taxes still apply to food. Under Act 2026-604 the state portion on food was suspended from May 1 to June 30, 2026.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable at the general rate except during the July back-to-school holiday (items of $156 or less in 2026).

otherRates.note: State sales and use tax rate on automotive sales.
Flat rate collected by eligible remote sellers in place of state and local use tax (§40-23-193(a)).
State lodgings tax; 5% in the 16 Alabama Mountain Lakes Area counties.

holidays2026.name: Severe Weather Preparedness Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: Held by statute on the last full weekend of February (Friday 12:01 a.m. to Sunday midnight): batteries, weather radios, flashlights, tarps, first aid kits and similar items (per-item cap adjusted for inflation since Act 2025-309; $94 per item and $1,564 for portable generators in the 2027 edition). Local participation varies.

holidays2026.name: Back-to-School Sales Tax Holiday
holidays2026.items: Clothing $156 or less per article; computers, software and school computer supplies, single purchase of $1,173 or less; school supplies, art supplies and instructional material $78 or less per item; books $47 or less. State tax only; local tax applies unless the locality opted in.

sales.holidayNote: Act 2025-309 indexes the holiday price caps to the Consumer Price Index and requires localities to adopt the exemption at least 90 days before the holiday weekend.

useTax.note: Consumers use tax is due at the same 4% general state rate (2% automotive, 1.5% machinery) on items bought without Alabama tax, plus applicable local use tax.

facts.text: The state food rate fell to 2% on September 1, 2025, after a cut from 4% to 3% on September 1, 2023.
Act 2026-604 suspended the state sales tax on food from May 1 through June 30, 2026; city and county food taxes were not affected.
Remote sellers in the Simplified Sellers Use Tax program collect a flat 8% instead of the combined state and local rate.
ALDOR administers over 200 city and county sales taxes, but not all; some localities collect their own tax directly.
Many cities also tax sales in their police jurisdiction outside city limits, usually at half the city rate.
Sales tax returns are due on the 20th of the month following the sales.

property.levied: Ad valorem tax levied on assessed value by the state, counties, municipalities and school districts; millage rates are set by county commissions and other taxing agencies.

assessment.text: Assessed value = appraised value x class ratio: Class I utilities 30%, Class II other property 20%, Class III owner-occupied residential, agricultural and forest 10%, Class IV private cars and pickups 15%. Since tax year 2025 (Act 2024-344), the taxable assessed value of Class II and III real property may rise by at most 7% a year; the cap resets on a sale or new improvement and runs through the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2027.
assessment.capText: Assessed value = appraised value x class ratio: Class I utilities 30%, Class II other property 20%, Class III owner-occupied residential, agricultural and forest 10%, Class IV private cars and pickups 15%. Since tax year 2025 (Act 2024-344), the taxable assessed value of Class II and III real property may rise by at most 7% a year; the cap resets on a sale or new improvement and runs through the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2027.

homestead.name: Homestead Exemption (H-1)
homestead.text: Owner-occupied single-family home on up to 160 acres: $4,000 of assessed value exempt from state tax and $2,000 from county tax (counties and cities may grant up to $4,000). Owners 65+ and disabled owners get larger or total exemptions (H-2, H-3, H-4).
homestead.applyBy: Apply at the county office; residence must be occupied on the first day of the tax year (October 1).

otherRelief.name: H-2 (65+ with AGI under $12,000, or retired disabled)
otherRelief.text: Exempt from all state property tax and $5,000 of assessed value of county tax, including school taxes.

otherRelief.name: H-3 (65+ with taxable income of $12,000 or less, or permanently disabled)
otherRelief.text: Exempt from all ad valorem taxes on the homestead.

otherRelief.name: H-4 (65+ with income over $12,000)
otherRelief.text: Exempt from all state property tax and $2,000 of assessed value on county taxes.

otherRelief.name: Current use valuation
otherRelief.text: Agricultural and timber land in Class III can be appraised on current use rather than market value on application.

dueDates.text: Property taxes become due on October 1 and are delinquent if paid after December 31.

facts.text: ALDOR's worked example: a $100,000 home x 10% = $10,000 assessed value; at 32.5 mills the tax is $325 before exemptions.
Owner-occupied homes are assessed at 10% of value, half the 20% ratio of commercial property.
Under Act 2024-344, taxable assessed value of homes and commercial real estate can rise at most 7% per year, starting with taxes collected from October 1, 2025.
A buyer's taxable value resets to full value after a sale, so the seller's tax bill is not a guide to future taxes.
Private passenger cars and pickups are taxed as property in Class IV at 15% of value.

uncertain: Effective date of the 4% general state rate not shown on the ALDOR rate page; effectiveSince left null.

The severe weather holiday dates for 2026 (Feb. 20-22) are derived from the statutory rule (last full weekend of February) stated by ALDOR; the 2026 per-item caps were not published on the page read (only the 2027 fact sheet: $94 / $1,564).
No further state food-tax reduction for 2027 found on ALDOR pages; not verified in the Code.
